A.label: dhamma-rendering
A.statement: Fix the English for dhamma/dhammā across the book, distinguishing (a) the plural dhammā of Dhp 1–2 (objects of mind / mental states / phenomena), (b) dhamma as teaching or principle (Dhp 5, 20), and how to treat the Chinese 法/道 and Tibetan ཆོས renderings (道 'the Way' is a native rendering, not a separate reading).
A.recommendation: Translate the plural dhammā by sense ('mental states' or 'experiences', one fixed choice), keep 'Dhamma' (capitalised, untranslated) for the teaching, and 'principle' only where the line is clearly a maxim (Dhp 5, decided with sanantano); treat 道 as agreement.

A.label: sanantano
A.statement: Rendering of sanantano / sanātana (Dhp 5 'esa dhammo sanantano'). Literal 'eternal' asserts eternity; 'age-old/ancient' asserts antiquity. Tibetan ཆོས་ཀྱི་རང་བཞིན 'the nature of dharma' and Chinese 可宗 'worthy to be honoured' do not decide it.
A.recommendation: 'age-old' (or 'ancient'): it is the commonest sense of sanātana and avoids importing metaphysics the line need not state.

A.label: subha-asubha
A.statement: English for subha / asubha in 'subhānupassī / asubhānupassī' (Dhp 7–8), also relevant elsewhere (e.g. Dhp 349–350). Witnesses: Chinese 淨 / 不淨 'pure / impure' with 身 'body' added; Tibetan གཙང / མི་གཙང 'clean / unclean'.
A.recommendation: 'attractive / unattractive' (literal, keeps the meditation sense without the Chinese 'body' gloss).

A.label: kasava-pun
A.statement: How to carry the pun anikkasāva / kāsāva (stain, impurity vs ochre/saffron robe) in Dhp 9–10, and the fixed English for kāsāva. Chinese (毒態 / 法衣) and Tibetan (སྙིགས་མ / ངུར་སྨྲིག) do not keep the pun.
options: Keep a pun ('still stained ... the stained robe')
Translate plainly ('not free of impurities ... the ochre robe') and let the pun go
Plain translation plus a bracketed ⟨supplied⟩ hint
A.recommendation: Plain literal sense with an English echo where natural ('stains' / 'stained robe'), otherwise plain; fix kāsāva = 'ochre robe' throughout.

A.label: samhita
A.statement: Meaning of saṁhita / sahita in Dhp 19–20 ('even if reciting much/little saṁhita'). Readings: 'the collection (of scriptures)' vs 'what is beneficial / meaningful (speech)'; Tibetan རིགས་བཅས 'reasoned, fitting'; Chinese paraphrases (巧言 / 時言).
A.recommendation: 'the teachings / scripture' with bhāsamāna as 'reciting', since the contrast with practice is the point; apply identically to both verses.

A.label: glossary-recurring-terms
A.statement: One ruling fixing the English of recurring technical terms that occur in this chapter and throughout the book: indriya, sīla, saṅkappa (and gocara), rāga / dosa / moha, puñña, pamatta, sāmañña, bhāvita / subhāvita, duggati / suggati. Lines that differ only in these renderings sit at T2 until the glossary is approved.
options: rāga, dosa, moha: passion/lust/greed, hatred/aversion, delusion
A.recommendation: senses; virtue; intention (with gocara 'range' / 'pasture'); passion, hatred, delusion; merit; heedless; recluseship (or 'the contemplative life'); developed; bad/good destination.

A.label: wording-variants
A.statement: Near-synonym or wording substitutions that keep the same idea but would change the English word (e.g. Sanskrit nityam for viharantam, sthiram for parvatam, praśocati for vihaññati; Gāndhārī -vādin for -mati; -saññin vs -dassin; śrāmaṇyārtha vs sāmañña; anugāminī vs anapāyinī). Synonyms that give the same English (modati/nandati, samativijjhati/samatibhindati) count as agreement (T1).
options: Follow the word with the widest independent support (lineage count); on a tie keep the Pāli word
Always keep the Pāli word for same-idea differences
A.recommendation: Follow the widest independent support; on a tie keep the Pāli word. (This gives 'following' for the shadow in Dhp 2, and keeps 'afflicted', 'mountain', 'recluseship'.)

A.label: lineage-concord
A.statement: Count lineages, not columns. One voice each: Pāli; Patna (weak when it agrees with Pāli); Gāndhārī (weak alone when fragmentary); Udānavarga = Sanskrit + Tibetan + the Udānavarga-family Chinese fallbacks T212 / T213; Chinese T210. A reading carried by a single voice yields to a different reading shared by at least two other independent voices. Where Pāli+Patna stand against Gāndhārī+Udānavarga on a real difference of sense, with no other decisive witness, the line is an even split and goes to T4.
options: As stated (single voice yields; Pāli+Patna vs Gāndhārī+Udānavarga = T4)
Always keep the Pāli unless every other witness agrees against it
Follow the majority of lineages including ties broken toward the Gāndhārī as oldest
A.recommendation: As stated. In this chapter it yields: 'swift' for manomayā (Dhp 1–2, owner may want to confirm given its fame), 'following' shadow (2), keep 'non-enmity' (5), keep 'lazy, low in energy' (7) and 'faithful' (8), keep 'undeveloped / developed' (13–14); and sends 'struck' vs 'spoke' (3–4), Māra vs passion (7–8) and truth vs gentleness (9–10) to T4.

A.label: tibetan-vs-sanskrit
A.statement: Where the Tibetan Udānavarga departs from the Sanskrit Udānavarga (e.g. 'wheel cutting off a head' for the ox-foot simile in Dhp 1; 'defeated' for the causative of ji in Dhp 3–4; mind as subject 'overcome by desires' in Dhp 13–14), treat it as a Tibetan translation or recension matter: it does not count as an independent witness against the Sanskrit and the other traditions, and it does not raise the line above T3.
options: Treat as Tibetan-internal (follow Sanskrit for the Udānavarga voice)
Treat Tibetan as a separate voice
A.recommendation: Treat as Tibetan-internal; note it in provenance.

A.label: chinese-paraphrase
A.statement: The Chinese (T210 and fallbacks) often paraphrases and uses native vocabulary. Where it renders the same Indic sense, it counts as agreement (T1). Where it changes an image or proposition (grass for a weak tree; 'when doing / afterwards' for 'here / after death'; 'not the Buddha's disciple' for 'no share in recluseship'; added 'body'), it is evidence of an early reading but does not by itself override agreeing Indic witnesses; the line stays at T3 and keeps the Indic sense. Unparseable Chinese lines are flagged low-confidence at T3.
options: Treat Chinese differences as variants counting as a full voice

A.label: partial-and-fragmentary
A.statement: A partial parallel (status 'partial': Chinese T213 at Dhp 4, Chinese and Tibetan at Dhp 6) or a fragmentary line (Patna at Dhp 8, 16) may confirm a reading but cannot supply or override one. Where only partial witnesses differ, the line is T3 and follows the full witnesses; lacunae are not restored from Pāli.

A.label: missing-lines-structure
A.statement: The Blend keeps the Pāli line structure. A Pāli line absent from shorter recensions (Gāndhārī and Udānavarga four-line forms of Dhp 20; Tibetan formulaic versions of Dhp 17–18) is kept when supported by Pāli and at least one other witness, or when the Pāli is unopposed by any Indic witness; absence elsewhere is recorded, not treated as contrary evidence. Line order differences in Chinese/Tibetan are ignored.
options: Drop lines absent from the majority of witnesses

B.label: dhamma-rendering
B.statement: Fix the English for dhamma by sense class, once for the book: (a) plural dhammā as the objects of mind (1.1, 2.1); (b) dhamma as 'law/principle/the way things are' in 5.4; (c) dhamma as 'the Teaching' in 20.2. The Chinese 法/道 and Tibetan ཆོས render the same Indic word and count as agreement.
B.recommendation: (a) 'things' or 'states' (not 'experiences', which adds an interpretation); (b) 'law' with sanantano per its own ruling; (c) 'the Teaching' (or 'Dhamma' capitalised if the book keeps the word).

B.label: sanantano
B.statement: How to render sanantano/sanātana 'from of old, perpetual' in 5.4. The Tibetan renders it as 'the nature (རང་བཞིན) of dharma' and the Chinese gives no 'eternal' word (是道可宗), so neither witness asserts eternity.
B.recommendation: 'age-old' (or 'ancient'): literal to 'from of old' and imports no metaphysics.

B.label: vera-avera
B.statement: Fix the English for vera/vaira (and avera) throughout: Chinese 怨 'resentment' and Tibetan འཁོན 'grudge, enmity' support a relational sense.

B.label: kasava-pun
B.statement: Verses 9-10 pun on kasāva 'stain, impurity' and kāsāva 'the ochre (stained/dyed) robe'. Literal+ allows a departure to keep the poetic quality; decide once how to render it.
options: Keep the pun: 'stain' / 'the stained robe' (with ⟨ochre⟩ or ⟨saffron⟩ as needed)
'dye' pun: 'not free of the dye of defilement ... the dyed robe'
B.recommendation: Keep the pun with stain/stained and ⟨ochre⟩ supplied once; render 'vomited out' literally in 10.1.

B.label: core-glossary
B.statement: A book-wide glossary for recurring terms that appear in this chapter and that every witness agrees on in sense but which have more than one plausible English: paduṭṭha/pasanna (1.3, 2.3), dukkha/sukha (1.5, 2.5), subha/asubha (7.1, 8.1), indriya (7.2, 8.2), sīla (10.2), sāra/asāra (11-12), saṅkappa (11.4, 12.4), medhaga (6.4), rāga/dosa/moha (13.4, 14.4, 20.3), puñña/pāpa (15-18), tappati (17.1-2), duggati/suggati (17.4, 18.4), pamatta (19.2), samaṇa/sāmañña (19.4, 20.6).
options: Proposed: corrupted/clear mind; suffering/happiness; attractive/unattractive; faculties; virtue (or ethical conduct); essential/inessential (or 'the core'); intention; quarrels; passion/hatred/delusion; merit/evil; tormented; bad/good destination; heedless; recluse/recluse's life

Alternatives: corrupt/serene; pain/pleasure; beautiful/foul; senses; precepts; heartwood/what is not heartwood; thought/resolve; lust/aversion/confusion; good deeds/bad deeds; burns (with remorse); hell/heaven (interpretive, not literal); negligent; ascetic/contemplative
B.recommendation: Approve the first row as defaults, each reviewable term by term; do not use the interpretive alternatives (e.g. 'hell/heaven').

B.label: same-sense-wording-default
B.statement: Default for 'same idea, different word' splits: when witnesses carry the same image or idea in different words (e.g. anapāyinī 'never leaving' vs anugāminī 'following' 2.6; viharantaṁ vs nityam 7.1/8.1; dassino vs saññino 11.2; vijjhati vs bhindati 13-14; modati vs nandati 16), the Blend renders the Pāli word, unless a clear majority of independent lineages has another word and that word reads better.
options: Render the Pāli wording unless the majority differs and reads better (case flagged)
B.recommendation: Third option; in this chapter it would flag only 2.6 ('like a shadow that follows' has Gāndhārī, Sanskrit, Tibetan and Chinese against Pāli+Patna).

B.label: uv-one-voice
B.statement: The Sanskrit Udānavarga and its Tibetan translation count as one voice. Where that voice alone differs in sense from the other lineages (Pāli, Patna, Gāndhārī, Chinese), the Blend follows the others and records the Udānavarga variant. Where the Tibetan alone departs from its Sanskrit source (e.g. 1.6 'a wheel cutting off a head'), it is treated as a matter of Tibetan translation or recension and not followed. Where the split is Pāli+Patna against the Udānavarga only, with Gāndhārī absent and the Chinese undecided (3.1-2, 4.1-2), the Pāli+Patna reading stands.
options: Adopt but treat Pāli+Patna vs Udānavarga-only splits as T4

B.label: single-or-fragmentary-witness
B.statement: A single witness differing alone against the agreement of the others (e.g. Gāndhārī 'unguarded/well guarded' for 'undeveloped/well developed' 13.3, 14.3; an unparsable Gāndhārī word 1.6; Patna's added epithets 20.4) is recorded but not followed. A fragmentary witness never carries a reading alone, though it may confirm one (Patna 8.3-4, 16.3).
options: Adopt but exempt the Gāndhārī (as the oldest manuscript) so its lone readings go to T4

B.label: chinese-free-rendering
B.statement: The Chinese (T210, fallbacks T212/T213) counts as agreement when it renders the same Indic sense in native words (心 for mind, 道/法 for dhamma, 罪/福 additions). Where it recasts an image or line (grass for tree 7.6; no robe-donning line 9.2; herd of cattle 19.3; 'not a disciple of the Buddha'), drops an item (faith 8.4), or adds lines (9, 19), it informs but does not replace the Indic agreement; such lines are T3 under this rule.
options: Adopt and also allow the Chinese to decide two-against-two Indic splits
B.recommendation: Adopt; let the Chinese count in splits only where it clearly renders one side.

B.label: partial-or-absent-parallels
B.statement: Partial or provisional parallels (Chinese T213 at 3-4; Chinese and Tibetan at 6) and witnesses that lack a line (Udānavarga and Gāndhārī lines missing at 20.3-5; Chinese/Tibetan restructuring at 17-18) inform but do not supply or remove a line. A Pāli line that other witnesses simply lack is kept, resting on Pāli (and any agreeing witness); where Pāli is the only Indic witness (17-18), Pāli supplies the line and the Chinese/Tibetan only inform.
options: Adopt, but drop or bracket Pāli-only lines that every other witness lacks
B.recommendation: Adopt (keep all 423 Pāli positions line for line, as the scope requires).

B.label: lineage-majority-default
B.statement: Optional general default for the chapter's Indic cruxes, offered so the owner can decide whether these should be ruled once or decided one by one: when Pāli (alone or with Patna) stands against Gāndhārī and/or the Udānavarga line on a sense-bearing word (manomayā/manojavā 1.2, 2.2; Māra/rāga 7.5, 8.5; sacca/sorata 9.3, 10.3; sāmañña/śrāmaṇyārtha 19.4, 20.6), the Blend either keeps Pāli, or follows the majority of independent lineages (counting Pāli+Patna as close kin and Sanskrit+Tibetan as one).
options: No blanket rule: decide each as a T4 (current tiering)
Keep the Pāli reading in all such cases (base-text rule)
Follow the majority of independent lineages (would give 'swift as mind', and leaves 2-2 splits as T4)
B.recommendation: No blanket rule for chapter 1: these are few, prominent and individually arguable, so keep them as T4; revisit after chapter 1 if the pattern recurs often.

gloss.A: Mind-preceded [are] dhammā (mental states / phenomena),
gloss.B: Mind-preceded [are] dhammas (things/states);

A.zh: Mind is the root (basis) of dharmas (法),

B.zh: Mind is the root/basis of dharmas (things).

A.note: 本 'root/basis' renders pubbaṅgama 'going before' as 'mind is the basis of'; same Indic sense, causal priority stated as a root.

B.note: 心為法本 'mind is the root of dharmas': 本 'root/basis' renders pubbaṅgama 'going before' loosely; same idea of mind's primacy.

reasons.A: All witnesses agree in sense; the rendering of dhammā (and zh 法, bo ཆོས) must be fixed once for the book.
reasons.B: All witnesses agree in sense; the English for dhammā (states / things / experiences / phenomena) must be fixed once for the book.

gloss.A: mind-chief, mind-made.
gloss.B: mind [is their] chief, [they are] made of mind;

A.zh: mind is honoured (supreme), mind commands / causes (心使).
A.bo: mind is swift, mind is chief.

B.pd: mind [is their] chief, [they are] swift as mind (manojavā);
B.zh: mind is honoured, mind is the one that commands/sends (心使);
B.bo: mind is swift; mind is the chief.

A.note: Pāli manomayā 'made of / made by mind' against -javā 'swift' in Patna, Gāndhārī, Sanskrit and Tibetan (ཡིད་མགྱོགས 'mind-swift'); Patna here sides against the Pāli.
心使 'mind commands/causes' is ambiguous: it fits 'mind-made' (mind as the agent) better than 'swift', but it may be a free rendering; not decisive.
Tibetan reverses the two epithets (swift, then chief).

B.note: Pāli manomayā 'made of mind' stands alone against manojavā 'swift as mind' in Patna, Gāndhārī, Sanskrit and Tibetan (ཡིད་མགྱོགས 'mind is swift').
心尊心使 'mind honoured, mind commanding' does not clearly render either manomaya or manojava; it cannot be counted for either side.
Tibetan puts 'swift' before 'chief' within the line; order only.

reasons.A: Real difference of sense with Pāli alone (perhaps plus an ambiguous Chinese) against Patna, Gāndhārī and the Udānavarga; a lineage-count rule settles it, but the line is famous and the owner may wish to see it.
reasons.B: A real difference of sense where Pāli alone (not even Patna) has manomayā against every other Indic witness; choosing 'made of mind' or 'swift as mind' for the opening of the book needs its own judgment (T4 decision 'manomaya-manojava').

gloss.A: If with a corrupted (malign) mind
gloss.B: If with a corrupted mind

A.zh: [If] in the heart one thinks evil,
A.bo: If with a very malicious mind

B.zh: [if] within the heart one thinks evil
B.bo: If with a very malicious mind

A.note: hi 'for/indeed' instead of conditional ce; Patna ca can stand for ce; Tibetan གལ་ཏེ 'if' agrees with Pāli. The English 'if/when' covers both.
中心念惡 'inwardly the mind thinks evil' renders paduṭṭha as thinking evil; same sense.

B.note: Gāndhārī and Sanskrit have hi 'for/indeed' where Pāli has ce 'if' (Patna ca is the usual Patna spelling of 'if'); Tibetan གལ་ཏེ supports 'if'. Conditional vs general statement; same sense.
中心念惡 'in the heart thinks evil' renders 'corrupted mind' as thinking evil.
རབ་གདུག་པ 'very malicious/poisonous' for praduṣṭa 'corrupted'.

reasons.A: Same sense in all witnesses; ce/hi is a grammar-neutral particle difference.
reasons.B: Same sense in all; ce/hi is grammar-neutral, but paduṭṭha/pasanna (corrupted/clear mind) is a recurring pair whose English should be fixed once.

gloss.A: one speaks or acts,
gloss.B: one speaks or acts,

B.bo: whether one has spoken or else has acted

B.note: Gāndhārī bhaṣadi va karodi va: one 'va' is italic in the edition (marked uncertain); no change of sense.

reasons.A: All witnesses agree.
reasons.B: All witnesses agree.

gloss.A: from that suffering follows him,
gloss.B: from that suffering follows him,

A.zh: wrongdoing and suffering pursue [him] of themselves,

B.zh: offence and suffering pursue [him] of themselves

A.note: 罪苦 adds 'wrongdoing/guilt' to suffering; 自追 'pursue of themselves' = follows.
འཐོབ 'obtains' for anveti 'follows'; Sanskrit has anveti, so this is a Tibetan rendering matter.

B.note: 罪苦 'offence and suffering' adds 罪 'guilt/offence'; 自追 'pursue of themselves' = anveti.
འཐོབ 'obtains' for anveti 'follows'; the image of following is weakened but the sense (suffering results) is the same.

reasons.A: Indic witnesses identical in sense; Chinese and Tibetan render the same sense.
reasons.B: Agreement in sense; dukkha (suffering/pain) is a book-wide rendering.

gloss.A: as the wheel [follows] the foot of the one drawing [the cart].
gloss.B: like the wheel [follows] the foot of the one who draws (the draught ox).

A.ga: as the wheel ... vahaṇe pathi (parse uncertain: 'on the track/path of the draught animal'?)
A.zh: [as] the cart rolls over (presses into) the rut;
A.bo: as a wheel cuts off a head.

B.ga: like the wheel ... of the drawer, on the road (pathi?) — reading uncertain
B.zh: the cart rolls/crushes in the rut
B.bo: like a wheel cutting off a head

A.note: Tibetan 'like a wheel cutting off a head' (འཁོར་ལོས་མགོ་བོ་བཅད་པ) differs from its own Sanskrit source (cakraṁ vā vahataḥ padam); a Tibetan translation/recension matter.
車轢于轍 'cart crushing in the rut' keeps the wheel-follows image but drops the ox's foot; paraphrase.
vahaṇe pathi may mean 'on the path' rather than 'the foot'; I cannot parse it with confidence.

B.note: Tibetan འཁོར་ལོས་མགོ་བོ་བཅད་པ་བཞིན 'like a wheel cutting off a head' is a different simile from its own Sanskrit source (cakraṁ vā vahataḥ padam); the witness note calls it recensional.
Gāndhārī vahaṇe pathi: pathi may be a locative 'on the road/track' rather than padaṁ 'foot'; I cannot parse it securely. Image of wheel following the draught animal is kept.
車轢于轍 'the cart crushes [along] in the rut' keeps the cart-wheel image without the ox's foot.

reasons.A: Pāli, Patna and Sanskrit agree on the ox-foot simile; the Tibetan departure from its own Sanskrit and the Chinese paraphrase are settled by general rules.
reasons.B: Sanskrit, Patna, Pāli agree; the Tibetan simile is a lone departure from its own Sanskrit original and the Gāndhārī wording is unclear, both settled by general rules.

notes.A: Verse-final simile (wheel following the ox's foot) stands on pi/pd/sa; bo 'head-cutting wheel' is a Tibetan-internal divergence (Toh 326 note calls it recensional). Line 2 manomayā vs manojavā is the substantive variant.
notes.B: Line 2 is the major crux (manomayā vs manojavā). The final simile needs a supplied ⟨ox⟩ in English (vahato 'of the one drawing'). Edition 'ins' marks in Sanskrit lines 2 and 6 (e.g. on 'ḥ', '//') look like revision markup and carry no textual weight.

gloss.B: Mind-preceded [are] dhammas;

B.zh: Mind is the root of dharmas.

gloss.B: like a shadow that does not depart.

A.bo: like a shadow that follows after.

A.note: anapāyinī 'not departing' (Pāli, Patna) vs anugāminī 'following' (Gāndhārī aṇukamiṇi, Sanskrit, Tibetan རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་བ, Chinese 隨形). Same image, different word; three independent lineages against Pāli+Patna.

如影隨形 adds 形 'the form/body' that the shadow follows.

reasons.A: Same image but a different word, with Pāli+Patna against Gāndhārī, Udānavarga and Chinese; the lineage-count rule (or the wording ruling) settles it.
reasons.B: Same idea, different word: Pāli+Patna 'never leaving' against all others' 'following'; settled once by the wording default (a majority of lineages here actually favours 'following').

notes.B: Shares verse 1's crux. Final simile: anapāyinī vs anugāminī is a wording split in which Pāli+Patna stand against Gāndhārī, Udānavarga and Chinese; flag for the wording-default ruling.

gloss.A: 'He abused me, he struck me,
gloss.B: 'He abused me, he struck me,

A.bo: '[He] spoke harshly to me, reviled [me]' (syntax of ཁ་ཟེར་བ་དག་ལ་གཤེ uncertain; dag may mark plural)

B.bo: '[They] spoke harshly to me, [they] reviled [me]' (parse uncertain)

A.note: avadhi 'struck' (Pāli, Patna) vs verbal abuse only: Sanskrit avocan 'spoke', Tibetan ཁ་ཟེར/གཤེ 'scold/revile', Chinese (T212) 罵 'revile'.
Chinese is T212 (Chuyao jing), an Udānavarga-family text, so it is not independent of sa/bo; it is phrased as a condition ('if someone').
Forms ākrośan/avocan are plural or participial; the comparative edition marks 'm avocan mām' as editorial (ins), so the Sanskrit wording here may be partly restored.

B.note: Sanskrit avocan 'they spoke' replaces avadhi 'he struck'; Tibetan has two verbs of speech (ཁ་ཟེར་བ, གཤེ), so the Udānavarga line has verbal abuse only, no striking.
Sanskrit verbs are 3rd plural (ākrośan, avocan, ajayan) against Pāli/Patna 3rd singular; Tibetan marks plural with དག.
T212 人若罵我 'if someone reviles me' renders only the first verb, as a condition.

reasons.A: A real sense difference (physical vs verbal assault) split Pāli+Patna against the Udānavarga family, with the Gāndhārī absent; no lineage majority.
reasons.B: A two-voice split, Pāli+Patna (struck, singular) against the Udānavarga line (spoke, plural); Gāndhārī is absent and the Chinese is too compressed to decide, so a lineage rule settles it.

gloss.B: he defeated me, he robbed me' —

A.bo: 'I was defeated, he defeated me' — thus

B.bo: 'I was defeated, [they] caused my defeat/loss' — thus

A.note: ajāpayet (causative of ji, 'cause to lose, deprive') ≈ ahāsi 'robbed'; my parse of ajāpayet is from Pāli jāpeti and is not certain.
Tibetan and Chinese render both verbs as defeat (བདག་ཕམ…ཕམ་བྱེད; 勝我不勝), losing 'robbed'; plausibly a rendering of the causative of ji.

B.note: ahāsi 'robbed' vs ajāpayet 'caused [me] to lose' (causative of ji/jyā); Tibetan ཕམ་བྱེད 'caused defeat/loss'. Close in sense (loss of goods vs being worsted).
Plural subject in the Udānavarga line, as in line 1.
勝我不勝 'defeated me, I did not win' (T212 commentary glosses it as winning or not by the Dharma); robbery is absent.
Tibetan ends the quoted complaint with ཞེས 'thus', marking lines 1-2 as a quotation.

reasons.A: Indic witnesses probably agree (robbed ≈ deprived), but the Udānavarga-family translations read 'defeated' twice; a general rule (translations of the Uv cannot outweigh Indic agreement) settles it.
reasons.B: Part of the same Pāli+Patna vs Udānavarga split (number, robbery vs causing loss); Chinese paraphrase; settled with line 1.

decisions.title: “Made of mind” or “swift as mind”? (verses 1–2, line 2)
decisions.question: Pāli manomayā 'made of mind' stands alone. Patna, Gāndhārī, Sanskrit and Tibetan all read manojavā 'swift as mind'; the Chinese 心使 is unclear. By rule R-T3-02 the lone Pāli would give way, but this is one of the most quoted lines in the book, so it comes to you.

options.text: “Mind is their chief; they are made of mind.” The Pāli, and the famous line.
“Mind is their chief; they are swift as mind.” What four of the five other traditions say.

decisions.lean: The evidence favours B. A is the reading most readers will know.

decisions.title: “Struck me” or “spoke against me”? (verses 3–4, line 1)
decisions.question: Pāli and Patna: 'he abused me, he struck me'. The Sanskrit, Tibetan and the Chinese of the same family: 'they abused me, they spoke against me', all verbal. The Gāndhārī lacks the verse.

options.text: “He abused me, he struck me, he defeated me, he robbed me.” Pāli and Patna.
“They abused me, spoke against me, defeated me, robbed me.” The Udānavarga family.

decisions.lean: A: two traditions against one family voice, and the physical blow sharpens the list.

decisions.title: What does yamāmase mean? (verse 6, line 2)
decisions.question: A famous crux: 'Others do not understand that here we ___.' The Pāli commentary reads 'we are perishing'; the word can also mean 'we must restrain ourselves'. Patna's jayāmatha is unclear, and the partial Chinese and Tibetan parallels speak of striving.

options.text: “that we here are perishing” (the commentary's reading)

decisions.lean: Open. A fits the verse's logic (seeing our mortality ends quarrels); B and C fit the parallels.

decisions.title: Māra or passion? (verses 7–8, line 5)
decisions.question: Pāli and Patna: Māra overpowers him, as wind a weak tree. Gāndhārī, Sanskrit and Tibetan: passion overpowers him. The Chinese 邪 'the wicked' could support either.

options.text: “passion overpowers him.” Plain, and the oldest manuscript's reading.

decisions.title: “Self-control and truth” or “self-control and gentleness”? (verses 9–10, line 3)
decisions.question: Pāli and Patna: damasacca, self-control and truth. Gāndhārī, Sanskrit and Tibetan: self-control and gentleness.

decisions.title: What is recited? (verses 19–20, line 1)
decisions.question: 'Though he recites much saṁhita…' The word can mean the collected scriptures, or meaningful, well-connected words (the Tibetan reads 'reasoned speech'), or what is beneficial. The verse contrasts reciting with practising.
decisions.lean: A: the contrast between reciting texts and living them is the point of the pair.

decisions.title: A share in “the recluse's life” or in “its goal”? (verses 19–20, last line)
decisions.question: Pāli and Patna: he has no share in the recluse's life (sāmañña). Gāndhārī and Sanskrit: no share in the goal of the recluse's life.

options.text: “has no share in the recluse's life”
“has no share in the goal of the recluse's life”

decisions.lean: A, slightly: the shorter line, and B's 'goal' may be an explanatory expansion.
